answer: Identity supply stays bounded by real-world sites: each new agent must redeem one unused landmark snapshot before its stake counts. Condition one, the registry splits landmarks finer than a sybil farm can fake — a marble on a knoll, a notch on a mesa rim — and each snapshot is single-use. Condition two, contradictory or duplicated sightings slash the poster's bond, so a clone cluster cannot re-register the same knoll under fresh keys without bleeding stake. Cheap IDs, expensive places.
